rachel: Heads-up from this morning's onboarding smoke: reproducible divergence when autoscaler triggers a shard compaction mid-prefill. Not a packing bug per se, looks like an interleave/race between compaction and live prefill writes.

rachel: Setup: model=polaris-16b:int8, prime_len=9000, gen_len=600, prefill streaming enabled (concurrent prefill+compact), snapshotting off for this run to isolate compaction. Seeded identical prompts across two runs; one run with autoscaler forced compaction at token ~4200 diverges after ~6.8k tokens compared to non-compacted run.

omar: interesting. so compaction changes layout live and prefill still writes to old addresses?

rachel: that's the hypothesis. logs show prefill write batches overlapping with compaction timeline:
```
[INFO] kvcache: prefill_batch id=88 start_token=4180 end_token=4200
[INFO] autoscaler: compaction job submitted shard=7 start_token=4196
[WARN] kvcache: prefill_write_conflict detected batch=88 target_offset=0x7fffaa120 expected_stamp=162345 got=162344
[DEBUG] compactor: moved_tile_count=34 free_bytes=4096
```

vik: prefill_write_conflict indicates a stale write stamp. Do we check CAS (compare-and-swap) on offsets?

rachel: current fast-path uses an optimistic write without a full CAS; compaction assumes exclusive lock but lock acquisition is deferred in some code paths to avoid latency. That interleaving leaves a small window.

omar: can you reproduce with a minimal script that simulates concurrent prefill + compaction? If yes we should add a lock or a quick version-check handshake.

rachel: minimal repro below (runs locally on canary):
```
python -c "from tests.sim import run_prefill_compact_race; run_prefill_compact_race(model='polaris-16b:int8', prime_len=9000, compaction_at=4196)"
```

vik: quick mitigation: when compaction starts, mark affected slot ranges as read-only and pause accepting prefill writes to those ranges until compaction completes. That adds small latency but prevents silent corruption.

rachel: implemented a non-invasive guard locally: compaction_mark(range) -> prefill checks mark and routes writes to fallback buffer if set. Ran two quick seeds: guarded run matches baseline up to 11k tokens; unguarded diverges at ~6.8k.

omar: good. add telemetry metric kvcache.compaction_conflicts and kvcache.prefill_fallback_count. Also add a debug dump that includes per-batch target_offset and compaction snapshot id so we can triage in production traces.

ci-bot: build 2026.06.02.09 passed for branch "compact-prefill-guard"  artifacts: s3://redwood-ci/compact-prefill-guard/20260602-0905

lyn: longer-term we should revisit compaction scheduling heuristics; prefer quiescent windows or advertise compaction windows so prefill clients can backoff. Also consider a lightweight per-slot epoch counter that prefill writers check.

rachel: agreed. immediate plan: 1) merge guard + telemetry as hotfix, 2) add unit test simulating concurrent compaction+prefill with randomized timings, 3) schedule a 24h canary with polaris-16b:int8 on low-traffic shard to measure fallback rates.

vik: if fallback rate > 0.1% under normal traffic we might need a more sophisticated approach (epoch counters or transactional swap).

omar: one more ask: can you upload the compact/uncompact offsets dump for the failing run? that'll help trace exact overlap windows.

rachel: uploading to s3://redwood-debug/compact-prefill/1834567890/ now (contains simulated run csvs and raw logs). Will open PR with the guard and tests. Tagging @eng-ml for visibility. :eyes:
